purpose: Every sentence that tells the patient to do something is an instruction claim: who does it, what they do, with what, where, and what they should see when done. A picture of a thing is not a picture of an instruction. While the how is unknown, the claim is a placeholder tied to an open question on the clinician's list, and the guide shows a pending marker on that frame.

statuses.placeholder: no picture yet shows the how; the guide shows a pending marker and the open question is on Song's list
statuses.text: the words carry the instruction fully, such as a phone number; no picture is needed
statuses.illustrated: a picture exists but no caption-blind observer has yet answered what to do from it
statuses.verified: caption-blind observers recovered what to do, with what, and where; a receipt is attached

claims.actor: the patient or a caregiver, at home
claims.tool: hands: untie the knot and unwind the gauze (pictured as an assumption; unconfirmed)

claims.note: A static four-panel card in the airline safety card style: dressing on, a hand drawing the gauze away with one arrow, bare head. In the live review of the redrawn card on 2026-09-18, all three observers read untie and pull away, the bandage and pad come off. The card as a whole failed on its tape panel, so this claim is illustrated rather than verified until the card passes again. The how pictured here is an assumption until Song answers.
claims.rule: instruction-picture rule; approved for now by John on 2026-09-18, Song's sign-off pending

claims.action: look at the incision behind the ear and decide whether tape covers it
claims.location: the incision in the crease behind the ear
claims.end_state: knowing which of the two care paths applies
claims.note: Panels 3 and 4 of the same card: the incision drawn as a line with short tape strips across it, magnified in panel 4 with the label Check for tape. In the live review on 2026-09-18 all three observers saw the strips across the line and read the panel as check that the strips are still in place. Two of three imagined a worried patient pulling the tapes or stitches off, a shared harmful misreading, so the card failed. Across fifteen observers in five reviews, most said the picture never says whether the tape stays on. The guide's text does not say either, so the fix waits on q.tape-after-three-days.
claims.rule: instruction-picture rule; approved for now by John on 2026-09-18, Song's sign-off pending
